body.p: The following remarks are made in response to the Action. In this Response, claim 1 has been amended. No claims have been canceled or newly added. Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 are pending. The claim amendments are supported by at least, for example, paragraph [0036] of the Specification as filed. There is no new matter.

Applicant submits herewith a Certification and Request for Consideration under the After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0 (AFCP 2.0). Applicant requests entry and consideration under the AFCP 2.0 guidelines.
Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over CN 208645329 ("Pei"). Applicant traverses the rejections.

Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to recite, "wherein the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link about the first axis by the hollow shaft." The Action states that Pei teaches the "second stage reduction assembly is adapted (via belt 24) to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link (relative to the second link) via the hollow shaft about the first axis." (Action at p. 3.) For at least the below reasons, Pei does not teach the above recited feature of amended claim 1.

Pei teaches the "first cantilever 20" includes the "[s]econd cantilever drive device includ[ing] servo motor 21, the second tooth belt driver and hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22, and servo motor 21 is installed at[] middle part of the first cantilever [20]." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Pei also teaches the "second tooth belt driver includes [] driving pulley 23, toothed belt 24 and passive belt wheel 25, driving pulley 23 [is] fixed on []axis of servo motor [21], passive belt wheel 25 is fixed on the input shaft of hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation (emphasis added).)
Although the "driving pulley 23" in Pei engages the "driving pulley 25" via the "toothed belt 24," Pei does not teach the "second cantilever drive device" of the "first

cantilever 20" causes the "second cantilever 30" to rotate as in claim 1. Instead, in Pei, the "hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22 is mounted on the front end of the first cantilever 20," and the "hollow type cycloidal-pin wheel" of the "speed reducer 22" teaches being fixed to the "input shaft [29] [and] is driven by servo motor 21 by the first tooth belt driver [24]." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation (emphasis added).) Accordingly, in Pei, the "first cantilever 20" is driven to rotate around the axis of the "input shaft 29" by the "servo motor 21" causing a rotation of the "input shaft 29" and the "hollow type cycloidal-pin wheel" of the "hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22."

Moreover, Pei does not teach the rotation of the "input shaft 29" of the "hollow cycloid reducer 22" causes rotation of the "second cantilever 30." Pei does not teach the "second cantilever 30" is fixed on the "input shaft 29" of the "hollow cycloid reducer 22." Instead, Pei teaches the "rear end 38 of the second cantilever 30 is fixed on the output shaft of hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation (emphasis added).) In Pei, the "servo motor 21" causing a rotation of the "input shaft 29" via the "second cantilever drive device" does not teach the "servo motor 21" also causes a rotation of the "output shaft" of the "hollow cycloid reducer 22."

Furthermore, it would not have been obvious for a person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) to arrive at the features of claim 1 based on Pei. Pei teaches the robot includes "hanger 10, [and] the first cantilever driving device." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Pei also teaches the "rear end 28 of first cantilever 20 is fixed on the output shaft of hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 12," and the "rear end 38 of the second cantilever 30 is fixed on the output shaft of hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Moreover, Pei teaches the "hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 12 input shaft by servo motor 11 pass through the first tooth driver drive." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.)

In Pei, the "hanger 10" is driven to rotate around the axis of the "hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 12 input shaft" by the "servo motor 11" driving the "first tooth driver drive." Similarly, the "driving pulley 25" of the "second tooth belt driver" in Pei is adapted to engage with the "driving pulley 23," and the "servo motor 21" causes a rotation of the "first cantilever 20" via the "input shaft 29" about the axis of the "input

shaft 29." For at least the above reasons, the Action fails to establish a prima facie case of obviousness regarding the above recited features of claim 1. Thus, Pei does not teach "wherein the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft about the first axis," as recited in claim 1.

Claim 1 further recites, "a hollow shaft extending along a first axis thereof and coupled to the first arm link, ... a second arm link connected to the hollow shaft." The Action states that Pei teaches a "hollow shaft (29) extending along a first axis (axis of 29) thereof and coupled to the first arm link, [and] providing a second arm link (20) connected to the hollow shaft." (Action at p. 2.) For similar reasons as those stated above, Pei does not teach this feature of claim 1. Specifically, Pei teaches the "hollow type cycloidal-pin wheel" of the "speed reducer 22" teaches being fixed to the "input shaft 29," and the "rear end 38 of the second cantilever 30 is fixed on the output shaft of hollow type cycloidal planetary gear speed reducer 22." Therefore, although Pei teaches the "first cantilever 30" is connected to the "input shaft 29," Pei does not teach the "second cantilever 30" is connected to the "input shaft 29." Thus, Pei does not teach "a hollow shaft extending along a first axis thereof and coupled to the first arm link, ... a second arm link connected to the hollow shaft," as recited in claim 1.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2- 4, 6, 8, and 9 are patentable over Pei. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness of the rejection with respect to features not discussed herein. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.

It is submitted that the rejections in the Action have been successfully traversed and that the application is now in condition for allowance. Reconsideration of the application and allowance thereof is solicited.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific allegation or comment of the Action does not signify agreement or concession with that part. Also, the arguments herein are not exhaustive.

The amendment or cancelation of a claim or other part of the Specification does not necessarily signify concession with an allegation or comment of the Action. Applicant reserves the right to prosecute the rejected claims in further prosecution of this or related applications.
